note: SHA-256 of the SCALAR half of SiteShellContract, JSON.stringify(sorted keys, null, 2), with RegExp values (e.g. contextualLinkRules[].keywordPattern) forced through String(v) via the stringify replacer. Both repos assert this: the main repo from build-plugins/articlesSiteShellBootstrap.ts, this repo from host/siteShellBootstrap.ts. These values render into every article <head>, so a drift between the two makes a fast-published page differ from the full build that later overwrites it. Functions are excluded (not comparable by value) — their behaviour is covered by the byte-identity renders instead. Re-recorded 2026-08-24 (main repo issue #6396): plain JSON.stringify serializes every RegExp to `{}` (no own enumerable props), so a keywordPattern source/flags edit never moved the digest — the fingerprint gave zero protection against regex-only drift between the two repos. The String(v) replacer fixes that; the digest form change is re-recorded in BOTH repos in this same coordinated change. Re-recorded for issue #8186 because the Offerwall registry now checks the active Firebase Auth persistence key instead of any project key; the value and digest were updated in both repos. RE-RECORDED AGAIN 2026-09-10, back to the pre-#8186 a8d61011… — NOT a revert of that behaviour. The #8186 digest was a function of a SECRET: the persistence key embeds the Firebase Web API key, which PR #1315 inlined into host/constants.ts and GitHub secret scanning then flagged (host/constants.ts#L66, commit c9bc65a4). This repo no longer holds that literal — the key comes from Firebase Remote Config through generator/scripts/load-rc-env.mjs, and host/tests/shell-contract-env.mjs zeroes VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY/FIREBASE_API_KEY so the digest stays a function of the SOURCE and not of whether the RC-loading step ran on this runner. Recorded here is therefore the key-free value, where the registry probes the `firebase:authUser:` prefix instead of the exact key: same question, same answer, no secret. With the key in the environment the emitted bytes are the site's exactly, so production output is unchanged. The site still records the key-bearing digest (its fallback is an obfuscated literal), so the two recordings diverge on purpose until the site drops its fallback too — declared in scripts/ci/loop-sync-manifest.json on the host/constants.ts entry.
